reed-bed.notes: Unequal curving reeds and low trough keep a clear contour at 160x112, 80x56 and 64x45. Waterline is subtle at smallest size; silhouette remains useful as a composition prop.

root-arch.notes: One root grips the left jamb and curves across the crown; exposed right stone and broad opening read clearly. Copper-brown living root remains distinct from stone and moss.

water-spout.notes: Connected ceramic pipe and continuous blue-green stream meet the basin. Thin water curve reads even compactly; water is a designed plane rather than transparent simulation.

moss-bench.notes: Thick seat, unequal legs and left moss cap keep a grounded asymmetric silhouette. The quiet opening underneath remains clear at compact size.

lily-cistern.notes: Broad rim, broken right edge, blue-green water and two unequal pads read at compact size. Simplified reflections distinguish the water from solid stone; no tactical-occupancy claim.

vine-trellis.notes: Tilted support and diagonal vine remain connected. Open lattice and leaf clusters are readable at 80x56; leaf detail simplifies at 64x45 without losing trellis identity.

seed-cabinet.notes: Unequal shelves, two terracotta trays and one climbing leaf read at 160x112 and 80x56. The cabinet is a scene prop, with no legible labels or invented contents.

stepping-culvert.notes: Two uneven slabs sit visibly on stone banks above an open water channel. Broad span-and-void relationship survives at smallest study size; the precise traverse is not a gameplay assertion.
